title: an inferred-fallible callback reaching a consumer as a shorthand PROPERTY NAME abbreviating a local must spell a Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': 'Public, abstract, ambient, and declaration-only contracts MUST express fallibility directly with `Result<A, E>` or `Promise<Result<A, E>>`.' A callback boundary is a VALUE edge, not an argument position: the callee invokes a function it received inside an object literal, an array literal, a parenthesis, a cast or a `new` argument list exactly as it invokes one passed directly. Fail-closed matters here because the accepting behaviour is silent and wrong rather than loud and wrong — R1FIX executed this class before the fix and measured `isOk() === true` with a `Result` sitting in the SUCCESS payload, with zero language diagnostics and zero emitted-TypeScript diagnostics. `{ transform }` and `{ transform: transform }` are the same program. This member of the class was fail-open on BOTH backends until 2026-08-25, and for the same reason on each: the shorthand's name node was reached by the walk, but resolving a symbol at that node yields the object literal's own PROPERTY symbol rather than the local it abbreviates, so the function reference resolved to nothing and the rule fell through silently. Both were fixed with the checker's dedicated shorthand accessor. It is the sharpest illustration of why a value-edge rule cannot be written as a syntax table: the byte-equivalent spelling one line away was refused correctly on both backends the whole time.
